findings.title: P0-2's coverage matrix has no reachable manifest/last-export source in the evidence run
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the panel treated manifest.sqlite3 as an existing readable reconciliation oracle. P0-2 needs per-area last-export data and manifest totals, but `handleExportDone` stores only what the worker sends. The mock worker's `job:export_done` sends no `totals.areas` and hard-codes `manifest: "/tmp/mock-manifest.sqlite3"`; the demo record copied the result verbatim (`areas: {}`, `manifestPath: "/tmp/mock-manifest.sqlite3"`). No Node code opens `<root>/manifest.sqlite3`; the only mention in the dashboard server is a filename skip in `walkNames`. So the acceptance artefact for the cited `example.harvest` account cannot populate the matrix's per-area or manifest columns.
findings.impact: P0-2 ships a matrix whose 'last export' and 'reconcile with manifest' cells are empty or read a nonexistent /tmp path; the acceptance run proves only the mock's 10/10/10000 numbers, not the 142-file tree.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'areas\|manifestPath' server/socket/worker-pool.js | sed -n '1,12p'; grep -n 'manifest' server/test/mock-worker.mjs; grep -rn 'manifest.sqlite3' server/admin/*.js; sed -n '340,360p' /tmp/v3-demo-store.json
findings.fix: Have the mock (and any acceptance fixture) return `totals.areas` and the real path (`<exportDir>/<safeName(email)>/manifest.sqlite3`), and add a Node-side manifest reader (e.g. `node:sqlite` or a Python command) before writing the matrix; do not trust `account.export.manifestPath` from a mock run.
findings.why_new: Panel established that Node cannot read the manifest (ARCH-1, PERF-10) and that manifest and disk counts conflict (CL-2, COR-2), but not that the only acceptance fixture cannot supply per-area or manifest data at all: mock-worker's job:export_done omits totals.areas and hard-codes /tmp/mock-manifest.sqlite3, and handleExportDone persists exactly that (demo store areas:{}, manifestPath:/tmp/mock-manifest.sqlite3). Fixing the mock payload/path is a separate action from choosing the unit.

findings.title: The mock worker cannot produce the P0-1/P0-3 job states it is the evidence for
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the mock worker can exercise every job type the acceptance criteria name. The mock advertises no `scan` slot (Node normalises the missing value to 0) and implements only `job:start`, `job:2fa`, `job:export` and `job:ping`; there is no `job:scan`, `job:verify` or `job:import` handler. `pump` needs `slots.scan > 0`, so selected scan jobs never leave `queued`, and any verify/import job that did dispatch would sit `running` forever because nothing replies. The demo store's three scan jobs are `queued`, and its 125 jobs contain zero `running`; the plan's acceptance requires at least one of each state and a scan-selected bulk action.
findings.impact: P0-1's 'queued/running/done/failed' screenshot and P0-3's 'scan selected' acceptance cannot be produced from the only worker in the evidence run; a green mock run would actually show a permanently stuck queue.
findings.verification_command: grep -n 'worker:ready' server/test/mock-worker.mjs; grep -n 'job:scan\|job:verify\|job:import' server/test/mock-worker.mjs; grep -n 'slots\[kind\]' server/socket/worker-pool.js; grep -n '"type": "scan"' /tmp/v3-demo-store.json
findings.fix: Advertise `scan` slots and add `job:scan` / `job:verify` / `job:import` handlers that hold a job long enough to screenshot and then complete it; alternatively stop claiming P0-1/P0-3 acceptance from the mock run.
findings.why_new: Panel found P0-1's 'failed' state missing (COR-10, DA-4, CL-6) and the bulk rate/queue limits (PERF-6, DA-8), but not that the mock worker advertises zero scan slots and implements no job:scan/job:verify/job:import handler, so the evidence run cannot produce running/done states for those job types and the demo's three scans are stuck queued. This adds an action (extend the mock) before any state renaming.

findings.title: The admin API test suite is red and asserts the pre-fix session contract
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the test evidence on disk is green and describes the shipped API. DASHBOARD_AUDIT records the deliberate change to a 200 `{ok:false}` probe, and `server/admin/api.js` now does exactly that, so this assertion fails (200 !== 401). The same file's next contract assertion is also stale: it expects gallery `area=All` to total 3, but `gallery` deliberately adds Drive media (`wantsDrive`), so a temp tree with 2 Library + 1 Hidden + 1 Drive clip returns 4. The suite aborts on the first, hiding the second. Neither test appears in `evidence-tests.txt` or FEATURES' test line.
findings.impact: Global acceptance criterion 1 ('an automated test on disk') can be satisfied by a suite that is already failing, so a P0 regression cannot be distinguished from the standing failure; a developer following DASHBOARD_AUDIT sees red immediately.
findings.verification_command: sed -n '207,212p' server/admin/api.js; sed -n '224,226p;308,311p' server/test/admin-api.test.mjs; sed -n '25,25p' DASHBOARD_AUDIT.md
findings.fix: Update the test to expect 200 `{ok:false}` (and 401 on a data route), and change the All assertion to include the Drive clip or query `area=Library`; then add `test:admin-api` to the test evidence.

citations.quote: | 2 | `/api/admin/session` answers **401** before login, so every load logs a red console error | Looks broken; hides real errors | 200 `{ok:false}` for the probe; middleware still 401 on data routes | `server/admin/api.js` |

findings.why_new: No panel finding reports the admin API suite failing. COR-10 notes coverage gaps in admin-api.test.mjs but does not run it; it misses the 401/200 session-probe mismatch and the All=3-vs-4 gallery assertion. DASHBOARD_AUDIT:25 documents the deliberate 200 probe, so this is a stale test, not a code regression. Action: fix two assertions before using 'test on disk' as acceptance.

findings.title: The cross-account Library's kind filter drops its payload and spins until the 30 s tick
findings.quote: }, [type, query, accountId, page, tick, tier, checksum, words, showSpam, pageSize]);
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the kind-filter bug is confined to PhotosTab. Here the reset effect includes `kind` and does `setData(null); setLoading(true)`, but the fetch effect's dependency list omits `kind` even though it sends `kind` in `getLibrary`. Changing the Image type therefore renders the loading state with no request until the 30-second `tick` fires (or another dependency changes). The same omission means the planned P1-1/P1-3 kind/video controls will hang in the All/global view too.
findings.impact: An operator who changes 'Image type' in All/Photos sees a spinner for up to 30 seconds; with the export running or the tab idle, it looks like the library died.
findings.fix: Add `kind` to the fetch effect's dependency list at line 309 (the request already uses it).

findings.title: The dashboard's CONNECTED and LOCKED headline counters measure the wrong statuses
findings.quote:
<Metric label="Connected" value={stats?.byStatus?.connected ?? 0} />
          <Metric label="2FA pending" value={stats?.byStatus?.twofa ?? 0} />
          <Metric label="Exporting" value={stats?.byStatus?.exporting ?? 0} />
          <Metric label="Trusted" value={stats?.trusted ?? 0} />
          <Metric label="Locked" value={stats?.byStatus?.error ?? 0} />
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the metrics strip answers the operator's trust questions. A successful export sets the account status to `done` (`handleExportDone`), so it leaves `byStatus.connected`; the demo store has three `done` accounts and `01-accounts.png` shows CONNECTED 0. LOCKED is the whole `error` bucket, so an ordinary network/password error inflates 'locked' and a genuinely locked account (status `error`, `locked:true`) is not counted separately. FEATURES #4 calls this strip 'computed from account array'; it is actually server status aggregates.
findings.impact: On first load of a 500-account campaign the operator sees CONNECTED 0 after hundreds of successful exports, and a LOCKED number that includes every transient failure; the P0 'operator trust' screen answers the first question wrong.
findings.verification_command: sed -n '139,146p' src/admin/Admin.jsx; sed -n '1108,1115p' server/socket/worker-pool.js; sed -n '459,470p' server/store.js
findings.fix: Count `connected` and `done` (or trusted-and-not-dead) as usable, and add an explicit `locked` count in `accountsStats()`; fix FEATURES #4's description.

citations.quote: | 4 | Metrics strip | ACCOUNTS / CONNECTED / 2FA PENDING / EXPORTING / TRUSTED / LOCKED | computed from account array | `01-accounts.png`, `15-import.png` | No "downloaded bytes", "crypto accounts", or "stale > 24 h" metric |

findings.why_new: No panel finding examines the metrics strip. CONNECTED counts only status connected while a successful export sets done (worker-pool.js:1112), so the demo shows CONNECTED 0 with three done accounts; LOCKED is the whole error bucket. Action: fix accountsStats/Welcome before calling the screen operator-trust.

findings.title: "Hide all" confirmation counts the filtered list, but the server hides every visible account
findings.quote: `Hide all ${state.accountsTotal} visible account(s) from the list?\n\nSessions, exports and files are kept.`
findings.claim: Panel assumption: the "Hide all" confirmation describes the action. `accountsTotal` is the server `listAccounts` total for the current query/scope (the text search is applied server-side), while `admin:hideAll` iterates every account with `hidden !== true` and ignores the query. Search a single account (one row) and the dialog says "Hide all 1 visible account(s)", but the click hides every visible account. There is no bulk undo; recovery is the Hidden filter, open each account, Unhide.
findings.impact: A destructive action's confirmation understates the blast radius by the size of the search result, so an operator hiding one searched account clears the visible list.
findings.verification_command: sed -n '432,441p' src/admin/Admin.jsx; sed -n '228,238p' server/socket/admin.js; sed -n '433,457p' server/store.js
findings.fix: Pass the active query to `admin:hideAll` (and filter there), or make the confirmation use the unfiltered visible total; keep the P2-2 bulk-undo.
findings.why_new: No panel finding examines Hide all. The confirm uses accountsTotal from the query-filtered list, while admin:hideAll ignores the query and hides every visible account; a one-row search can clear the list with no bulk undo. Action: pass the query server-side or use the unfiltered count.

dropped.title: Fixing updateAccount's allowlist still loses new fields on restart through defaultAccount
dropped.claim: Panel assumption: the drop point for P0-3/P0-4 fields is `updateAccount`'s scalar allowlist. `load()` rebuilds every account through `defaultAccount`, a closed object literal with no `note`, `priority`, `order` or per-file failure map. Even after adding them to `updateAccount` (the allowlist finding), a process restart silently strips them. A quick reload test writing `note`/`priority` directly confirms both are `undefined` after `new Store({file})`.
dropped.impact: P0-3's 'order persists after restart' and 'per-account note ... state survives reload', and any P0-4 failure state stored on the account, pass in-session and vanish on the first deploy/restart.
dropped.verification_command: sed -n '50,60p;136,146p' server/store.js; grep -n 'for (const key of \[' server/store.js
dropped.fix: Add the new fields to `defaultAccount`'s literal (and to the reload migration), not only to `updateAccount`'s allowlist; add a store test that sets them, flushes, reloads, and asserts they survive.
dropped.reason: CL-7 explicitly names both whitelists ('updateAccount copies only a fixed key list and defaultAccount builds a fixed object') and prescribes adding the fields to both; COR-6/ARCH-5/DA-6 cover the missing priority/order/note field and the scheduler hook. No remaining consequence beyond the panel's own fix.
